goals: Implement durable rejected-attempt reuse for Supervisor runs. Add optional RunTaskState fields attemptWorktree, attemptBranch, attemptBaseCommit, attemptStartedAt and attemptRejectedAt with backward-compatible validation. When runCodexBatch receives a runManifest, checkpoint the exact worktree/branch/base before starting the worker. Retain a rejected dirty worktree even without --keep-worktrees; retain its attempt fields on rejection; clear them on acceptance. Add CodexBatchOptions reuseAttempts. On supervisor resume --retry-rejected, reuse a valid rejected attempt by default, accept --reuse-attempt as the explicit default assertion, and add --fresh-attempt to force a new worktree; reject conflicting flags. Fail closed on an invalid recorded attempt unless fresh was requested. Validate the path is under <repo>/.cliyard/worktrees, is a registered git worktree, branch matches, HEAD equals the recorded base, and attemptRejectedAt is present. Expose reusable attempts in supervisor status JSON and human output. Add an end-to-end focused test proving a fake worker writes a draft and exits 1, its worktree survives, default resume reuses the same path and sees the draft, fresh retry gets a different path, and tampered metadata fails closed. Do not change progress telemetry or runtime drill files.
nonGoals: No concurrent attach to an interrupted active worker

goals: Close the runtime-drill abnormal-child cleanup gap. When a drill child times out or exits abnormally after starting services, terminate the child with SIGTERM then a bounded SIGKILL escalation, wait until it is gone, and run the existing exact orphan executor against that scenario's scratch control root. Persist an abnormalRecovery section in runtime-failure-drills.json and re-run the normal manifest/log/process/port checks after recovery. Fail the drill if the executor reports needs_human or any service/port remains. Never signal an unproven service group directly. Add a test-only environment hook that makes a child hang after readiness, use a short child timeout in a focused test, and prove the child was killed, recovery completed, cleanup is complete, the service process/group is gone, the port is free, and the failed child cannot be reported as accepted. Keep normal and timeout paths distinct and documented in code.
nonGoals: No change to global reaper ownership rules
